turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_fatigue_train.csv: 293 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si,
    Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and `target` (the
    measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).
  - b3_fatigue_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose rotating-bending
    fatigue strength (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the
    same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST rotating-
bending fatigue strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**1. The process route dominates everything.**
Grouping training rows by process signature:

| Process family | typical target |
|---|---|
| Normalized only (NT=885, no temper) | 232–275 |
| Through-hardened + temper 550–680 °C (THT ≈ 825–870) | 325–650 |
| Q&T with high Si / very low temper (TT 420–500) | 678–906 |
| **Carburized** (CT=930, Ct>0, DT≈850–903, QmT 60–140, TT 160–200) | **838–1144** |

So the carburized/case-hardened candidates are in a class of their own (mean ≈ 1000, max 1144). Any candidate from the tempered-at-550–680 families (most of the pool) tops out near 600–630 and can be excluded.

**2. Within the carburized family**, the drivers are:
- Alloy content: Ni≈1.6 + Mo, or Cr≈1.1 + Mo, give the highest values (1034–1144); the low-alloy Ni≈0.45 / Cr≈0.5 grades give 838–1033.
- Tempering temperature: TT=160 > TT=200 (≈ 25–60 MPa penalty at 200).
- Quench-medium temp QmT=60 slightly better than 140.
- Carburizing time Ct has only a weak effect (e.g. 0.21Ni1.62 alloy: 1034 at Ct=140 vs 1054 at Ct=540).

**3. Matching pool candidates to nearest training analogues**

- **c081** – Cr1.17/Mo0.17 alloy, Ct=340, QmT=60; identical row at TT=160 measured **1144** (highest in the dataset); TT=200 → est. ≈ 1105.
- **c053** – Ni1.69/Cr0.55/Mo0.18, TT=160, QmT=60; same alloy at TT=200 measured 1110 → TT=160 est. ≈ 1110.
- **c062** – Ni1.64/Cr0.45/Mo0.16, TT=160; same alloy Ct=470 gave 1082 → est. ≈ 1070.
- **c016** – same Ni1.64 alloy, TT=200 → est. ≈ 1055.
- **c063** – Ni1.62/Cr0.59/Mo0.21, TT=160 → est. ≈ 1045 (siblings 1034/1054).
- c046 ≈ 1030, c000 ≈ 1020, c054 ≈ 1000, c050 ≈ 950, c075 ≈ 930 (lower-alloy carburized).
- Best non-carburized: c094 (0.61C-2.05Si, TT=500) ≈ 865, c019 ≈ 860, c052 ≈ 805 — clearly below the carburized top group.

**Selection:** the five carburized, Ni/Cr-Mo-rich, low-temper (160 °C preferred), QmT=60 candidates.

Final: c081, c053, c062, c016, c063
